If an Italian citizen previously received an IEC Working Holiday Work Permit for 6 months, are they eligible to now apply for a Working Holiday Work Permit for 1 year, since the program recently increased the duration of the validity from 6 months to 1 year?
For example, an Italian citizen had a Working Holiday Work Permit for 6 months, that has now expired. They currently hold a Young Professionals Work Permit. Will they be able to apply for a Working Holiday Work Permit for year after their Young Professionals Work Permit expires?
Thank you!

Question: If an Italian citizen previously received an IEC Working Holiday Work Permit for 6 months, are they eligible to now apply for a

For example, an Italian citizen had a Working Holiday Work Permit for 6 months, that has now expired. They currently hold a Young Professionals Work Permit. Will they be able to apply for a Working Holiday Work Permit for year after their Young Professionals Work Permit expires?
Response: As of November 1, 2022, Italian citizens may participate in International Experience Canada twice, in any category. The validity period for the Working Holiday stream also increased from 6 months to 1 year.
Under the IEC program, there are requirements specific to each country or territory that holds a bilateral agreement or arrangements with Canada's lEC program. In the case of Italy, applicants are allowed 2 participations only. However, foreign national youth are also eligible to apply through an IEC recognized organization twice in their lifetime and repeat category participations through a RO are allowed. Which means, that for an Italy applicant, they are allowed 2 participations under the terms of the youth mobility arrangement (YMA) with Canada and 2 participations through a recognized organization.

threads.subject: Work hours for International Students -- REP-2023-2075 --
threads.question:
Hello, If an international students takes paid sick leave or paid vacation leave, do these hours count towards the 20 hour a week off campus work limit? Thank you,
and Citizenship Caneda
Ghazal, Reda (IRCC/IRCC)
threads.answer:
Question: If an international students takes paid sick leave or paid vacation leave, do these hours count towards the 20 hour a week off campus work limit?
Response: Off campus hours are defined as any time the study permit holder spends earning wages or collecting a commission, even if they are on call during these hours and not actually working. This would include being on paid sick leave or paid vacation leave.
Please visit How many hours you can work off campus for more information.
We hope that this information is helpful to you.
